steps.title: Introduction to Stir Fry
steps.content: Stir frying is a quick cooking technique that originated in China. It's perfect for busy weeknights when you want a flavorful, healthy meal in minutes!

steps.title: Prepare Your Ingredients
steps.content: Cut all vegetables into uniform, bite-sized pieces. This ensures everything cooks evenly. Have all ingredients ready before you start cooking.
steps.noteText: Cutting vegetables on the diagonal (bias cut) creates more surface area and helps them cook faster.

steps.title: Make the Sauce
steps.content: Combine soy sauce, a splash of rice vinegar, minced garlic, and a touch of sugar. A good sauce is the foundation of a delicious stir fry.
steps.noteText: Add a teaspoon of cornstarch to your sauce to help it thicken and coat the ingredients better.

steps.title: Heat the Wok
steps.content: Heat your wok or pan until it's very hot before adding oil. This prevents sticking and gives food that authentic 'wok hei' flavor.
steps.noteText: If you don't have a wok, a large flat-bottomed skillet works well too. Just make sure it's hot before adding ingredients!

steps.title: Cook in the Right Order
steps.content: Start with aromatics (garlic, ginger), then add protein, followed by vegetables (hardest to softest), and finally the sauce. Toss continuously while cooking.
steps.noteText: Don't overcrowd the pan or your ingredients will steam instead of stir-fry. Cook in batches if necessary.

steps.title: Serve Immediately
steps.content: Stir fries are best enjoyed right away while hot and fresh. Serve over steamed rice or noodles for a complete meal!
steps.noteText: Garnish with fresh herbs like cilantro or sliced green onions for extra flavor and presentation points.

steps.title: Introduction to Spring Rolls
steps.content: Fresh spring rolls are a healthy, customizable appetizer or light meal with roots in Southeast Asian cuisine.

steps.title: Step 1: Prepare the Fillings
steps.content: Wash and julienne vegetables like carrots, cucumber, and bell peppers. Cook and cool protein if using.
steps.noteText: Using a mandoline slicer makes getting thin, uniform vegetable strips much easier and faster.

steps.title: Step 2: Soften Rice Paper
steps.content: Fill a large, shallow dish with warm water. Dip one rice paper wrapper for about 5-10 seconds until pliable but not too soft.
steps.noteText: Don't soak the rice paper too long - it will continue to soften as you work with it!

steps.title: Step 3: Fill and Roll
steps.content: Place fillings on the bottom third of the wrapper, fold in sides, and roll tightly from the bottom up, like wrapping a burrito.
steps.noteText: Place a few fresh herb leaves (mint, basil, cilantro) facing down first so they show through the wrapper for a beautiful presentation.

steps.title: Step 4: Make Dipping Sauce
steps.content: Mix hoisin sauce with peanut butter, a splash of water, and crushed peanuts for a classic Vietnamese-style dipping sauce.
steps.noteText: For a Thai-style dipping sauce alternative, try sweet chili sauce mixed with a bit of lime juice and fish sauce.

steps.title: Introduction to Fattoush
steps.content: Fattoush is a vibrant Lebanese salad made with fresh vegetables, crispy pita, and a zesty dressing. Let's learn how to make it step by step!

steps.title: Step 1: Prepare the Vegetables
steps.content: Chop tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, lettuce, and green onions into bite-sized pieces. Freshness is key!
steps.noteText: If you are rushed by time or unable to chop the ingredients with a knife, you could try using a food processor.

steps.title: Step 2: Toast the Pita
steps.content: Cut pita bread into small pieces and toast or fry until golden and crispy. This adds the signature crunch to Fattoush.
steps.noteText: Feel free to adjust how long the bread should be fried for! If you prefer something less crunchier, fry it for a shorter duration of time!

steps.title: Step 3: Make the Dressing
steps.content: Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, garlic, salt, and pepper. Sumac gives Fattoush its tangy flavor.
steps.noteText: Use the best quality extra virgin olive oil you can find and avoid those simply labeled as "Pure", they lack character and flavor

steps.title: Step 4: Toss & Serve
steps.content: Combine veggies, pita, and dressing. Toss well and serve immediately for the best crunch. Enjoy your homemade Fattoush!
steps.noteText: If you think you make too much of a mess when tossing the ingredients, try using a lid! Make sure to give enough space for the food to toss around though

steps.title: Introduction to Tzatziki
steps.content: Tzatziki is a refreshing Greek yogurt dip with cucumber, garlic, and herbs. Perfect as an appetizer or side dish!

steps.title: Step 1: Prepare the Cucumber
steps.content: Grate one cucumber and squeeze out excess moisture. This prevents the dip from becoming watery.
steps.noteText: Use a cheese cloth or clean kitchen towel to really get all the moisture out of the cucumber.

steps.title: Step 2: Mix the Base
steps.content: In a bowl, combine 2 cups of Greek yogurt with 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 tbsp olive oil.
steps.noteText: Full-fat Greek yogurt works best for authentic flavor and creamy texture.

steps.title: Step 3: Add Herbs & Seasonings
steps.content: Mix in cucumber, 2 tbsp fresh dill, 1 tbsp fresh mint, salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon juice.
steps.noteText: Don't skimp on the fresh herbs - they make all the difference in flavor!

steps.title: Step 4: Rest & Serve
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving to let flavors meld. Enjoy with pita bread!
steps.noteText: Tzatziki tastes even better the next day, so consider making it ahead of time.

steps.title: Introduction to Hummus
steps.content: Hummus is a creamy Middle Eastern dip made from chickpeas, tahini, and olive oil. Let's make this versatile and nutritious dish!

steps.title: Step 1: Prepare the Chickpeas
steps.content: Drain and rinse one can of chickpeas. For ultra-smooth hummus, remove the skins.
steps.noteText: Warm chickpeas blend more smoothly. Microwave them for 30 seconds before blending.

steps.title: Step 2: Blend Base Ingredients
steps.content: In a food processor, combine chickpeas with 1/4 cup tahini, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 2 cloves of garlic.
steps.noteText: Add ingredients in this order: tahini and olive oil first, then chickpeas for the smoothest texture.

steps.title: Step 3: Add Flavors
steps.content: Add juice from 1 lemon, 1/4 tsp cumin, salt, and 2-3 tbsp water. Blend until smooth and creamy.
steps.noteText: Add ice water instead of room temperature water for a fluffier texture!

steps.title: Step 4: Serve with Style
steps.content: Transfer to a bowl, create a well in the center, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and chopped parsley.
steps.noteText: Let hummus rest for an hour before serving to develop flavors, and serve at room temperature.
